brief: Cooler-than-expected PCE, flattered by a methodology change (Supercore PCE actually rose fastest in months on an 'Other Services' jump), cut October Fed hike odds to 37%, half the level of two days earlier. That corroborates Fed's Williams, who said only one more hike is needed late this year. Despite that, the 10Y yield rose to 5.30%, a 7th straight month of rising yields. The 1-month real 10Y move (+57bp) breached Goldman's 2-standard-deviation 'speed limit' (about 50bp) that Goldman links historically to negative equity returns. Goldman's Pasquariello says the rule 'was just triggered,' and historically every such move has hammered stocks, but not this time, as investors keep holding mega-cap, memory and semiconductor names. Goldman's Privorotsky flags oil falling the same day rates rose as the bigger risk for stocks. Beneath the index, breadth is collapsing: the median stock is down 5% over the month, the equal-weight S&P fell a 7th straight week, a streak seen only in 2002 and 2022, and credit is cracking, with CCC junk bond spreads at 998bp on the data-center debt buildup. Rabobank's Michael Every recaps Q3: global bond yields rose sharply, G20 central banks kept hiking, and oil jumped from $73 to $104.
